| Stage | Typical Time | Notes |

## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-blind: since 10 May 2021 the reviewer is unaware of the author's identity and the author of the reviewer's (https://jrai.net/article-review-policy/, retrieved 2026-11-23). Papers must be fully anonymised, with an anonymised title for the document file; the response-to-reviewers letter must be anonymised too because reviewers see it (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. Not stated on the pages read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. Not stated. The editorial letter that accompanies reviews is described as listing what revisions must address (https://jrai.net/editorial-process/) |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Not a number. The page says stages of review, decision and resubmission may repeat until a final decision, and that revised papers go back to further review unless revisions are very minor, commonly to at least one of the initial reviewers (https://jrai.net/editorial-process/, retrieved 2026-11-23). The author guidelines say most published papers were substantially revised after review (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Outcomes after review are: rejected, revise and resubmit, accepted subject to minor revisions, or accepted; the page says the latter is very rare after initial reviews and that revise and resubmit or reject are most common. The editorial team sends the title and abstract of every paper to all editorial-board members, who comment on fit and propose reviewers; the team aims for 2 to 4 reviews and may pick at most one reviewer from the author's suggestions (https://jrai.net/editorial-process/) |

Sources: https://authorservices.wiley.com/ethics-guidelines/index.html (Wiley preprints section) and https://authorservices.wiley.com/asset/Article_Sharing_Guidelines.pdf (Wiley sharing chart, read by text extraction; its layout is not recoverable from the text). The journal's copyright agreement, which sets the accepted-manuscript embargo, was not read.

The journal requires double-blind review, so a manuscript already posted under the author's name defeats anonymity (inference from the review model, not a stated rule) |

## Format

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Papers (articles) on any branch of anthropology; book and film reviews and review essays (commissioned; offers and enquiries go to the Reviews Editor, completed reviews to the Publications Officer); an annual competitively selected Special Issue; virtual issues collecting previously published work (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/, https://jrai.net/book-and-film-reviews/, https://jrai.net/submit-an-article/ and https://jrai.net/about-the-jrai/, retrieved 2026-11-23). The journal says it features original ethnographic research and asks authors not to submit papers that are only summaries or non-ethnographic or non-academic in nature |
| **Word limit** | 10,000 words including the abstract, notes and bibliography (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/, retrieved 2026-11-23). An older publisher guidelines copy (dated 2021-04-14) added "unless permission for a longer submission has been granted in advance by the Editor"; that sentence is not on the current page |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Not stated on the current page. The older copy dated 2021-04-14 (https://web.archive.org/web/20210414063203/https://rai.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/journal/14679655/forauthors.html) allowed longer submissions with advance permission from the editor |
| **Abstract limit** | Up to 200 words; keywords are not required (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/, retrieved 2026-11-23). The abstract should be comprehensible to a non-specialist |
| **Reference limit** | No separate limit; the bibliography counts toward the 10,000 words. Initial submissions need no specific formatting beyond double spacing, standard 12-point font; accepted papers follow the JRAI reference guide, whose 2026 style sheet specifies UK -ize spelling, single quotation marks, endnotes and author-date references (https://jrai.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/JRAI-STYLE-SHEET-2026.docx, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Supplementary material** | Blank. Not addressed on the pages read |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No numeric limit stated on the current page. Permission for reproduced material is required before publication, not at submission (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/) |

### Orientation

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Ethnography-led theorising. The journal says its core focus has traditionally been social anthropology, that many papers develop theoretical interventions on the basis of ethnographic research, and that it also publishes ethnographically informed theoretical interventions (https://jrai.net/about-the-jrai/, retrieved 2026-11-23). Among the 405 OpenAlex articles of 2021 to 2026 with an abstract, "ethnograph-" appears in 175 (43.2%) and theory words in 56 (13.8%); regexes in Methodological Preferences |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Qualitative and interpretive work dominates by keyword: quantitative or statistical terms 3 of 405 (0.7%) and "survey" 3 (0.7%), against "ethnograph-" 175 (43.2%) and "fieldwork" 60 (14.8%) (OpenAlex abstracts, counted 2026-11-23). The aims page says biological-anthropology papers may use quantitative, qualitative or mixed methods (https://jrai.net/about-the-jrai/) |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | Aims text names social, linguistic and biological anthropology and archaeology, and work from other disciplines that relates to anthropology's core interests, with preference for work of broad anthropological interest (https://jrai.net/about-the-jrai/). In the abstract sample: archaeology 16 (4.0%), biological terms 11 (2.7%), linguistic 8 (2.0%) |

## Soft Metadata

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

> Evidence layers: OpenAlex works for this source dated 2021 to 2026 (1,186 records, of which 458 are of type article and 405 of those have an abstract = 88.4%; retrieved 2026-11-23; counts use the abstract-bearing articles as denominator); the journal's own aims, guidelines and board pages. Keyword regexes are in Methodological Preferences and Sensitive Topics.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Author countries of the 458 OpenAlex articles dated 2021 to 2026 (articles with at least one author in the country; a paper can count for several): United Kingdom 170, United States 93, Germany 29, Australia 24, Canada 22, Denmark 21, France 10, Netherlands 10, Norway 9, Singapore 8; 27 articles carry no country in OpenAlex (counted from the OpenAlex works records, retrieved 2026-11-23). The journal says it is international in scope (https://jrai.net/about-the-jrai/) |
| **Editorial-board geography** | 33 editorial-board entries on https://jrai.net/editorial-board-structure/ (retrieved 2026-11-23), counted by the country printed in each entry: United Kingdom 16, United States 8, and one each in Belgium, Austria, France, Netherlands, Canada, Panama, Mexico and Brazil, plus one entry ("University of Oxford") with no country printed (16+8+8+1 = 33). The editor-in-chief is at the University of Kent (UK); the archaeology associate editor is in Germany |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | The author guidelines tell authors to "think beyond the canon of Anglophone scholarship" (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/, retrieved 2026-11-23; quote of 7 words) and expect ethnographic and archaeological case studies to engage regional literatures and work beyond Euro-American traditions; the aims page encourages engagement with voices marginalised from the mainstream canon of Anglophone scholarship (https://jrai.net/about-the-jrai/). Keyword counts in 405 abstracts: "indigenous" 25 (6.2%); colonial, decolonial or settler terms 20 (4.9%) |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Counts in 405 abstracts: gender and sexuality terms 35 (8.6%); race and racism terms 1 (0.2%); see Sensitive Topics for regexes. No editorial statement on diversity topics beyond the marginalised-voices wording above |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | No school is named. Most-cited articles dated 2021 to 2026 in OpenAlex (retrieved 2026-11-23): "Introduction: Towards an anthropology of data" (https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9655.13477, 130 citations); "Children of the palms: growing plants and growing people in a Papuan Plantationocene" (https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9655.13489, 102); "How is it between us? Relational ethics and transcendence" (https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9655.13496, 67); "Feral ecologies: the making of postcolonial nature in London" (https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9655.13653, 60); "The cognitive origin and cultural evolution of taboos in human societies" (https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9655.14098, 52). The list mixes data, multispecies, ethics and cognitive-evolutionary work; it is a citation list, not a statement of editorial leaning |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** The journal asks that title and abstract make clear how the paper contributes new insights on topics of broad anthropological interest, that the conceptual contribution be stated and sustained, and that papers not be summaries or non-ethnographic (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/, retrieved 2026-11-23). The editorial process page says papers are rejected before review when the anthropological contribution is insufficiently broad or unclear (https://jrai.net/editorial-process/).
- **What kind of engagement?** Contribution framed as a positive insight rather than a gap, empirical cases contextualised in regional and local literatures, theory related reflexively to the case, methods explained "even if briefly" (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/, tips section). Papers should be comprehensible to a non-specialist in the area (same page). The aims page says empirical research is encouraged but papers must develop an argument beyond the cases presented (https://jrai.net/about-the-jrai/).
- **Article types and length**: papers up to 10,000 words, book and film reviews, review essays, an annual competitive Special Issue (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/, https://jrai.net/special-issues/).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: three recent special issues: "Nightmare Egalitarianism", "Beyond Public Reason" and "Ageing Time Beings", each organised around a concept. "Nightmare Egalitarianism" names case studies from Amazonia, Burma, Georgia, India, Malawi, Morocco and the Ancient Near East; "Ageing Time Beings" names ethnographic insights from Canada, Denmark, India, Japan, Kyrgyzstan, Uganda and the USA; "Beyond Public Reason" describes a concept and forms of deliberation (community organizing, legal argumentation, spiritual claims, solidarity) and names no regions or ethnography in its description (https://jrai.net/special-issues/, re-read 2026-11-23). Proposal windows for 2027 and 2028 are closed and reopen in December 2026 for the 2029 issue (same page).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: about 40% of submissions are rejected before review, for being outside the core remit, for an unclear or insufficiently broad contribution, or for insufficient empirical basis or nuance (https://jrai.net/editorial-process/, retrieved 2026-11-23). The guidelines also say papers are often rejected because the analysis lacks nuance (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/).

### Methodological Preferences

> Method counts are over the 405 OpenAlex articles dated 2021 to 2026 that have an abstract (458 articles in all; https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=primary_location.source.issn:1359-0987,publication_year:2021-2026, retrieved 2026-11-23), matching title plus the abstract rebuilt from OpenAlex's inverted index, case-insensitive. In the regexes below, `\|` inside a table cell is a literal alternation bar `|` (escaped only because of the markdown table). Shares use 405 as the denominator. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. The schema's rows were written mainly for psychology and HCI; where a row does not fit anthropology the cell says so, and rows were added for fieldwork, archival, archaeological, biological, linguistic and visual work.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 1 (quantitative methods in general; no experiments counted) | Regex `\b(?:quantitative\|statistical\|statistics\|regression\|survey data)\b`: 3 (0.7%); regex `\bsurveys?\b`: 3 (0.7%). Experimental designs were not counted separately. The aims page welcomes quantitative, qualitative or mixed-methods empirical papers in biological anthropology (https://jrai.net/about-the-jrai/), but the counts show them in few papers |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | Regex `\binterview\w*`: 12 (3.0%); `\bqualitative\b`: 2 (0.5%). The row fits poorly: the dominant qualitative mode is ethnography, not named interviews (next row) |
| Ethnography / fieldwork (added row) | 4 | Regex `\bethnograph\w*`: 175 (43.2%); regex `\bfield-?work\b\|\bfield research\b`: 60 (14.8%); `\bparticipant[- ]observation\b`: 4 (1.0%, score 1 on its own). A 4 is allowed because the journal states it "features original ethnographic research" and asks authors not to submit non-ethnographic papers (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Regex `\bauto-?ethnograph\w*`: 0 of 405 |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | Regex `\btheor(?:y\|ies\|etical\|ize\|izing\|izations?)\b`: 56 (13.8%). The aims page says it also publishes theoretical interventions where they are ethnographically informed (https://jrai.net/about-the-jrai/) |
| Archival / historical (added row) | 2 | Regex `\barchiv(?:e\|es\|al)\b`: 7 (1.7%) gives the score. Regex `\bhistor(?:y\|ies\|ical)\b` matches 70 (17.3%, which would score 3), but history words also mark topics rather than methods, so it is not used for the score |
| Archaeological (added row) | 2 | Regex `\barchaeolog\w*\|\barcheolog\w*`: 16 (4.0%); the aims page says archaeology is published where clearly related to broader anthropological issues (https://jrai.net/about-the-jrai/) |
| Biological / evolutionary (added row) | 2 | Regex `\b(?:genetic\|genomic\|ancient DNA\|isotop\w*\|skeletal\|bioarchaeolog\w*\|primate\w*)\b`: 11 (2.7%); a cognitive-evolutionary article is among the most cited (https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9655.14098) |
| Linguistic (added row) | 2 | Regex `\blinguistic\b\|\blanguage ideolog\w*\|\bsociolinguistic\w*`: 8 (2.0%) |
| Multimodal / visual (added row) | 2 | Regex `\b(?:multimodal\|film\|video\|podcast\|photograph\w*\|visual)\b`: 11 (2.7%) |
| Mixed methods | 0 | Regex `\bmixed[- ]methods?\b`: 0 of 405 |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 0 | Regex `\bmeta-?analy\w*\|\bsystematic review\b`: 0 of 405. The row does not fit the field's usual forms |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. Count: of the 405 OpenAlex abstracts of 2021 to 2026, 232 (57.3%) contain a first-person pronoun by regex `\b(?:I\|my\|me\|we\|our\|us)\b` (case-sensitive; plural "we" and "our" can be a co-author team or generic; counted 2026-11-23). Examples among the latest-indexed abstracts: "I hope" (https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9655.70259), "I noticed" (https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9655.70211), "Here we address" (https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9655.70216), "Here we consider" (https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9655.70215). The guidelines give no rule on first person |
| **Expected density** | Papers up to 10,000 words including abstract, notes and bibliography (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/, retrieved 2026-11-23). The guidelines tell authors to "show, don't tell": exemplify ideas through concrete cases, give voice to research subjects, signpost connections, and spell out theoretical terms (same page, tips section). 367 of the 458 articles (80.1%) have one author, 40 two, 17 three and 14 four or more; 20 records list no authors (OpenAlex authorship lists, counted 2026-11-23) |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Abstract of up to 200 words, comprehensible to a non-specialist; keywords are not required (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Writing style notes** | Initial submission: double spaced, standard 12-point font. Accepted papers: the 2026 JRAI style sheet (UK -ize spelling, single outer quotation marks, series comma, endnotes, author-date references with alphabetical order and semicolon between citations; https://jrai.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/JRAI-STYLE-SHEET-2026.docx, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Authorship pattern** | See Expected density: 80.1% single-author among all 458 articles (OpenAlex, 2026-11-23) |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages do show.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |

| **Dominant tradition** | Board entries do not carry a subfield label, so none is counted. Titles show structure: the editor-in-chief, an archaeology associate editor, a biological-anthropology associate editor and a reviews editor, with 33 board members; the editorial-process page says the title and abstract of every paper go to all board members for comment and reviewer suggestions. The aims page says the journal's core focus has traditionally been social anthropology | https://jrai.net/editorial-board-structure/ ; https://jrai.net/editorial-process/ ; https://jrai.net/about-the-jrai/ (retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Reviewer list size** | Blank. No reviewer list is published on the pages read. The editorial team is 1 editor-in-chief, 2 associate editors, 1 reviews editor, 2 editorial assistants and 1 publications officer; the board has 33 entries. The editors aim for 2 to 4 reviews per paper | https://jrai.net/editorial-board-structure/ ; https://jrai.net/editorial-process/ |
| **Review model** | Double-blind since 10 May 2021; reviewers should not be close colleagues or have close personal relationships with the author, though previous professional relationships are not seen as a barrier; no paper is assigned to a team member with a conflict of interest | https://jrai.net/article-review-policy/ (retrieved 2026-11-23) |

| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Blank. Keyword counts do not suggest a quantitative-leaning corpus (ethnograph- 43.2% against quantitative 0.7%), but how reviewers treat work cannot be read from counts | OpenAlex counts, see Methodological Preferences |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Authors must confirm at upload that they have obtained ethics clearance from their university for the research and have tried to conduct and represent research ethically and respectfully; authors whose institution has no review process, including independent scholars, are invited to contact the journal (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/, disclaimers section, retrieved 2026-11-23). Wiley's general rules on consent and approval also apply (https://authorservices.wiley.com/ethics-guidelines/index.html) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are the large majority: 367 of 458 articles (80.1%) in OpenAlex for 2021 to 2026 (counted 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | The ethics-clearance statement explicitly recognises that its model may not apply to independent scholars and invites them to get in touch (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/, retrieved 2026-11-23). No other independent-scholar rule found |
| **Data transparency requirement** | None on the journal's pages (searched the saved text of the guidelines, submission, review and process pages for "data availability" and "data sharing": no hits). Wiley's policy says all research published in its journals must include a Data Availability Statement (https://authorservices.wiley.com/ethics-guidelines/index.html, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-blind review requires a fully anonymised manuscript, an anonymised document title and an anonymised response-to-reviewers letter (https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/, retrieved 2026-11-23). The author statement requires the manuscript to be original, unpublished and not under review elsewhere, in whole or in part |
| **AI use** | Allowed with disclosure under Wiley's policy; AI cannot be an author (https://authorservices.wiley.com/ethics-guidelines/index.html, retrieved 2026-11-23); see AI Policy |
| **Open access and cost** | Gold and green options; APC USD 4330 per Wiley's price list (https://authorservices.wiley.com/asset/Wiley-Journal-APCs-OnlineOpen.xlsx, updated 12 October 2026, read 2026-11-23; options per https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/) |
| **Platform change** | Since 30 October 2025 articles are processed in Wiley's Research Exchange; earlier submissions stay in Editorial Manager (https://jrai.net/submit-an-article/, retrieved 2026-11-23). The journal says it cannot give feedback on manuscripts before submission but will give general guidance on fit through the Editorial Assistant (same page) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Length**: papers over 10,000 words including abstract, notes and bibliography fall outside the stated limit (Format; https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/).
- **Anonymisation**: double-blind review needs a fully anonymised manuscript, document title and response-to-reviewers letter (Peer Review; same page).
- **Originality and exclusivity**: the author statement requires an original, unpublished text not under review elsewhere, in whole or in part (Practical Concerns; same page).
- **Ethics clearance statement**: authors confirm ethics clearance from their university at upload, with a route to the editors for those without such a process (Practical Concerns; same page).
- **Scope**: papers outside the core remit or non-ethnographic in nature are rejected or discouraged (Framing Requirements; https://jrai.net/editorial-process/ and https://jrai.net/author-guidelines/).
- **AI use**: undisclosed substantive AI use breaches the Wiley policy (AI Policy).

### Soft Tax

- **Pre-review screening**: about 40% of submissions are rejected before review (Desk Rejection Rate; https://jrai.net/editorial-process/), so the title and abstract carry the first judgement; the title and abstract go to all board members for fit comments.
- **Revision cycles**: acceptance straight after the first reviews is very rare, and resubmissions are usually reviewed again (Peer Review; https://jrai.net/editorial-process/); the publisher prints a 2025 median of 455 days from submission to acceptance (Review Cycle Time; real browser 2026-11-24).
- **Open access cost**: APC USD 4330 per Wiley's price list of 12 October 2026 (Open Access).
- **House style**: accepted papers are reformatted to the JRAI style sheet, with UK -ize spelling and endnotes (Voice & Style).

### Best Suited For

- Ethnographically grounded theoretical argument aimed at a broad anthropological readership: the journal states it features original ethnographic research, and "ethnograph-" appears in 43.2% of 405 abstracts (Methodological Preferences; Framing Requirements).
- Papers that engage regional literatures and scholarship beyond the Anglophone canon: stated in the author guidelines (Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Religion, violence, gender and Indigenous topics in ethnographic form: religion terms 19.0%, violence and gender 8.6% each, Indigenous 6.2% of 405 abstracts (Sensitive Topics).
- Authors who can accept double-blind review and a clearly stated ethics-clearance declaration; independent scholars are explicitly invited to discuss that statement (Practical Concerns).
- Special-issue proposals for 2029, with the window reopening in December 2026 (Publication Frequency).

### Not Recommended For

- Quantitative, experimental or systematic-review work with no ethnographic or conceptual argument: quantitative terms 0.7%, meta-analysis terms 0 of 405 (Methodological Preferences). This reflects frequency, and the aims page does welcome quantitative biological-anthropology work.
- Non-ethnographic summaries or narrowly specialist papers: the journal asks authors not to submit summaries or non-ethnographic work and wants broad anthropological interest (Format; Framing Requirements).
- Anyone who needs a measured turnaround: only the journal's aims and a publisher block of unstated basis exist (Review Cycle Time).
- Papers that cannot be anonymised (Hard Blockers).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [American Anthropologist](american-anthropologist.md) | Also a Wiley-published society journal accepting social, archaeological, biological and linguistic work; its entry records an 8,000-word limit with references counted, so a JRAI manuscript of 8,000 to 10,000 words needs cutting first; also author-anonymised review |
| 2 | [Current Anthropology](current-anthropology.md) | Broad four-field venue; its entry records limits of 6,000 to 10,000 words for major articles and a commentary-and-reply format that JRAI does not use |
| 3 | American Ethnologist (Wiley; no entry in this corpus) | Not read; named only because it appears on the same Google Scholar Metrics Anthropology list (rank 15, h5-index 22; https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=top_venues&hl=en&vq=soc_anthropology, fetched 2026-11-23) |
